newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bombers in air, unknown if headed to Iraq - CNN.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bombers in air, unknown if headed to Iraq - CNN.

text.p: U.S. Air Force B-52 bombers carrying cruise missiles are in the air, but it was unknown if they were headed for Iraq, CNN reported on Monday.
They took off from bases in Guam, CNN reported, citing a Pentagon source. It said the source could not say if the planes would be used in an attack on Iraq.

A senior military official told CNN the planes left the bases hours ago, but said because of the long flying time from Guam to the Gulf the planes would have been launched before any final decison on military action was made.
CNN reported there was no confirmation of any attack taking place.

The United States said on Monday Iraqi troops appeared to be moving deeper into Kurdish opposition-held territory in northern Iraq, and President Bill Clinton had readied a "course of action" in response.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry, speaking with reporters as the president campaigned in Wisconsin, said there was evidence that some of the Iraqi forces that overran the Kurdish stronghold of Arbil over the weekend were "penetrating deeper" into northern Iraq.
